policy_context.positive_axis_definition: Clean FMO support requires flavin-dependent O2 activation to a C4a-(hydro)peroxyflavin or equivalent flavin-peroxy oxygenating intermediate, followed by substrate oxygen insertion or oxygenation.
policy_context.minimum_support_policy: No primary promotion or countable benchmark change is allowed before at least six non-duplicate clean FMO rows plus explicit hard-negative separation and human/import-gate approval.

summary.bottom_line: CHMO, HAPMO, and human FMO1 pass the hard-negative screen as source-admissible non-import-ready external leads. OTEMO and KMO remain duplicate/leakage holds from prior source-free terminal evidence. Salicylate 1-monooxygenase is chemically FMO-compatible but held as same-family aromatic hydroxylase support already represented by m_csa:131 and m_csa:551.

candidate_gate_results.source_mechanism_signal: FAD/NADPH Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenase; reduced flavin reacts with O2 to support C4a-peroxyflavin/Criegee oxygen-transfer chemistry and lactone-forming oxygen insertion.

gate_conclusions: Do not import, relabel, retrain, alter thresholds, or change production scoring from this artifact.
Treat uniprot:P12015, uniprot:Q93TJ5, and uniprot:Q01740 as the only non-duplicate external leads from this six-row gate.
Keep uniprot:H3JQW0 and uniprot:O15229 on duplicate_hold because prior terminal duplicate/leakage decisions remain controlling.
Keep uniprot:P23262 on duplicate_hold because it corroborates the already-covered aromatic hydroxylase lane rather than adding a new evidence axis.
All six candidates remain non-countable and non-import-ready without source-free geometry/materialization, duplicate/leakage terminal review where missing, import gates, and human approval.
